data.title: Path Traversal
data.summary: A filename taken from the request was used to build a filesystem path without constraining it to the intended directory, so traversal sequences reached files elsewhere on the host — configuration, credentials and keys among them.
data.description:
Path traversal is a containment failure: the application means "a file in this directory" but implements "this path, relative to this directory", and `../` walks out of it.

What that yields depends on the account the service runs as, but the usual targets are predictable: application configuration holding database credentials and API keys, `/etc/passwd` to confirm the flaw and enumerate accounts, SSH private keys, cloud credential files, and application source code, which often reveals further flaws.

Filtering for `../` is not sufficient. Encoded forms, double encoding, mixed separators on Windows, and sequences reassembled after a first pass of stripping all defeat naive filters.
data.recommendation:
* Resolve the path to its canonical form and confirm it is still inside the intended base directory before opening it.
* Prefer an indirection layer: accept an identifier, look up the real path in a map, and never use client input in the path at all.
* Run the service as an account with no read access outside the directories it needs.
data.short_recommendation: Resolve paths and confirm they stay inside the base directory.
